chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding
the rotten water: you may perform wudu from it, unless you find other water, in which case you should avoid it.

key_terms.الماء الآجن: Rotten or stagnant water — water that has changed in smell, taste, or color due to stagnation
key_terms.تتوضأ: You perform wudu — ritual ablution required before salat
key_terms.تنزّه: Avoid/turn away from — to maintain distance from something undesirable

ai.seo_question: Can you perform wudu with rotten or stagnant water in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that wudu is valid when performed with stagnant or rotten water (al-ma' al-ajin) if no other water is available. However, if clean water can be found, one should turn away from the rotten water and use the clean alternative. This ruling reflects a principle of permissibility under necessity in Islamic jurisprudence (rukhsa), balancing ritual validity with hygiene considerations.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>:
‘Regarding the rotten water, you can perform Ablution (Wudhu) from it unless if you were to find the water other than it, so you turn away from it’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘
Is it permissible to take Wudu’ with water which is discolored?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You can do so but if you find other water cleanse yourself with it.’”
